title: Grateful Dead Live at Reno Centennial Coliseum on 1982-03-13
lineage: MAC > Nakamichi CR-5A > Edirol FA-66 > Wavelab 2448 > CD-Wave (24bit output) > R8Brain > TLH > FLAC 1644 tagged. Transferred by Andrew F. 08/2015
source: AUD: Nakamichi CM300/CP4 shotguns > Sony TC-D5M > Maxell XLII (S1) and Hitachi ME-Metal (S2). Set up FOB, recording by Brian Schley.

ai_review.summary: Excellent audience recording of a solid 1982 show highlighted by a blistering Stranger > Franklin's > Estimated > Eyes sequence and Jerry’s poignant vocals.
ai_review.review: The tape captures a vibrant 1982 performance with a strong first set (notably “Bertha” and “It Must Have Been the Roses”) and an incendiary second set featuring a smoking Stranger‑Franklin’s‑Estimated‑Eyes medley. The audience recording is praised as clear and lively, making it a worthwhile upgrade for fans of this underrated era.

ai_rating.rationale: One detailed 5‑star review emphasizes both an outstanding musical performance and high‑quality audience recording; the lack of multiple reviews limits confidence but the consistent praise warrants a high rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Described as a great audience recording that serves as an archive upgrade, implying clear capture of crowd ambience and instrument balance.

standout_songs: It Must Have Been the Roses
show_quality.setlist_flow: First set strong with solid classics; second set blistering and tightly sequenced, featuring a creative segue from Space into ‘Truckin'’ using a Dear Prudence reference before moving into Black Peter.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Poignant vocals and soulful solo noted as especially moving; guitar work praised on Franklin's Tower and Eyes of the World.
